body:
Apologies to @wjt, it seems there was some overlap with this PR and mine, which got merged: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/124163

I searched issues but didn't think to search PRs, I actually stumbled across this while searching for a *different* issue related to AudioStreamInteractive.

> As I re-read this PR, I wonder if this line is wrong in the FADE_CROSS/FADE_IN state. Wouldn't we expect the target clip to fade in over the end of the filler clip, for symmetry with FADE_CROSS/FADE_OUT meaning that the source clip fades out over the start of the filler clip? But I haven't actually tested it.

(As an aside: it seems you can work around this by fiddling with the "beat count" import setting on the filler clip.)

My team has been running into several usability issues like this with AudioStreamInteractive. We are trying to implement the features and fixes we need internally, but some of them go beyond the scope of easy PRs. It may be worth a proposal to overhaul AudioStreamInteractive (perhaps in a similar way to the TileMap -> TileMapLayer rework, to avoid breaking changes?).

I'm delighted that your fix has been merged - I'll be able to clean up my workaround in our game.  I may later rebase this patch anyway because I think deduplicating the logic is a nice cleanup, but I'll close for now.

(I'm sure you know but in case not: if you join the Godot Contributors chat you can find the audio team there, who at least the last time I dipped my toe in would meet roughly fortnightly. Unfortunately I have not had the time I had hoped to to do more work in this area but if your team does, I suggest syncing with that group.)
